lines: {target}? Empty End stone gives no comfort.
If anyone heads for End Barrens, this is my advice. Keep away from edges and watch the sky.
The void makes silence feel heavier.
End Barrens is no small story.
I will remember End Barrens as bare End land with nothing friendly in sight.
My first preparation for End Barrens would be telling someone the route.
I would bring steady light and enough food to turn back from End Barrens.
I would listen harder whenever the road went quiet near End Barrens.
I would rather return from End Barrens with a plain story than a fresh wound.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at End Barrens.
The mention of End Barrens puts blocks for bridging and a spare pick at the top of my list.
With one missed step above the void nearby, a loose tool head becomes more than a nuisance.
I would keep some strength in reserve in case of an enderman blocking the narrow way, even if the way ahead seemed quiet.
The End darkness is no place to balance a loose rivet on one knee.
I would mark the bridge leading toward the gateway before anyone stopped at a platform with a back wall to repair gear.
Before you return to End Barrens, tell me what failed so I can fit the next set properly.
I would choose a tight grip over a perfect edge for work around End Barrens.
I expect the gear from End Barrens to bring a lesson back to my workshop.
A spare handle is light compared with a broken-tool walk back from End Barrens.
Which tool needed attention first when you returned from End Barrens?
{target}? High End ground still ends in void.
If anyone heads for End Highlands, this is my advice. Mind bridges and do not chase anything floating.
Chorus fruit grows where falling is easy.
End Highlands is no small story.
I will remember End Highlands as high ground that does not feel safe.
The village should know my route before I travel to End Highlands.
Food, torches, and a clear head belong in any pack for End Highlands.
A quiet stretch is when I would grip the tools tighter near End Highlands.
I want any tale of End Highlands to end at home with supper.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at End Highlands.
I keep coming back to chorus forests rising across broad end-stone ridges. That would make me keep the return gateway marked.
With the possibility of an enderman blocking the narrow way, repair work belongs at home, not halfway there.
The End darkness would hide small damage, so I would inspect the gear before leaving.
If we lost the bridge leading toward the gateway, I would want the tools to make another way.
Crossing the end edge of End Highlands with an open tool roll would be asking to lose half of it.
A tool returning from End Highlands earns a full check at my bench.
After hearing about End Highlands, I'd oil the iron and test every wedge twice before leaving.
I want a look at the tool marks from End Highlands. They may explain the parts you skipped.
For End Highlands, I'd bring wedges, cord, and enough iron for one ugly repair.
That story changes what I would put in the pack for End Highlands.
{target}? Even the middle of the End feels lost.
If anyone heads for End Midlands, this is my advice. Mark your way and distrust the horizon.
There is no village smell in that air.
End Midlands is no small story.
I will remember End Midlands as End stone stretching where roads should be.
Before visiting End Midlands, I would make sure someone expected my return.
Good provisions matter more than a heavy pack on the way to End Midlands.
The calm moments would keep me watchful during a trip to End Midlands.
I would make room for the story, not another scar from End Midlands.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at End Midlands.
I keep coming back to rolling end stone hiding gaps between higher islands. That would make me check each ridge before choosing a bridge.
Blocks and a pick with a tethered grip would earn a place in my pack at End Midlands.
A spare pick matters when one missed step above the void cuts off the simple plan.
With the possibility of an enderman blocking the narrow way, repair work belongs at home, not halfway there.
The End darkness would hide small damage, so I'd inspect the gear before leaving.
I would not send gear back out after End Midlands without looking over every joint.
Bring me the worn gear from End Midlands sometime. Damage remembers details that people miss.
After hearing that story about End Midlands, I would give everyone one useful tool. Then nobody has to carry the whole workshop.
Hearing that, I would pack differently before going to End Midlands.
Once everyone is home from End Midlands, someone should check the grips. Sweat, water, and fear all loosen things.
{target}? Small islands feel smaller beside the void.
If anyone heads for Small End Islands, this is my advice. Bridge slowly and never look proud near an edge.
End stone gives no second chances below it.
Small End Islands is no small story.
I will remember Small End Islands as little bits of ground with forever around them.
Before a trip to Small End Islands, someone at home should know my route.
I would rather carry a careful pack than a proud one into Small End Islands.
The peaceful parts would not lower my guard around Small End Islands.
I would leave the treasure behind before leaving a friend at Small End Islands.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Small End Islands.
Hearing about tiny islands forcing one bridge after another makes me want to build rails before looking over the edge.
If Small End Islands is the destination, more blocks than the route seems to need belongs in the pack.
I would rather repair gear under good light than struggle through the End darkness.
The bridge leading toward the gateway matters more than the perfect repair when trouble is moving closer.
The small edge of Small End Islands would tell me which tool stays packed and which one stays ready.
I am already reconsidering which tools belong on a trip to Small End Islands.
I'd rather carry one tool fitted for Small End Islands than five chosen in a hurry.
Around Small End Islands, I'd trust a plain tool that fits the hand over a fine one that slips.
The wear on your tools may fill in whatever the story left out about Small End Islands.
At Small End Islands, everyone should carry one useful tool. Then nobody has to carry the whole workshop.
{target}? Victory there still feels far from home.
If anyone heads for The End, this is my advice. Don't anger the tall ones and keep away from the void.
End stone does not smell like any living place.
The End is no small story.
I will remember The End as a pale world with no proper village sound.
I would not leave for The End until someone knew where I was headed.
My pack for The End would hold food, light, and nothing chosen for pride.
The silence around The End would make me check the path twice.
Nothing found at The End matters more than bringing everyone home.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at The End.
Once you mention the obsidian pillars leaving the dragon room to attack from anywhere, my first thought is to keep the exit portal in mind during the fight.
I'd make room for a pick for the crystals' cages and blocks for cover before setting out for The End.
If I had to face one missed step above the void, I would want every tool tested first.
I'd oil and wrap the iron before trusting it to the End darkness.
I'd test my footing on the edge of The End before swinging anything heavy.
At The End, the best field repair is the one you prepared before leaving the bench.
I wonder what the repairs from The End will teach me at the bench.
For another trip to The End, good equipment should make hard work possible, not make foolish work safe.
A keen tool is useful at The End. A loose handle makes it useless fast.
The return from The End feels longer when a snapped handle leaves the iron useless.
{target}? Nothing below is not the same as safety.
If anyone heads for The Void, this is my advice. Stay away from edges like they owe you emeralds.
There is no road back from falling forever.
The Void is no small story.
I will remember The Void as empty dark where even warnings feel small.
I would tell someone the plan before taking one step toward The Void.
For The Void, I would choose food and torches before anything impressive.
I would treat the quiet parts seriously around The Void.
The best account of The Void ends with everyone back in the village.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at The Void.
Hearing about empty distance swallowing tools, blocks, and people alike makes me want to stop building before the supply runs thin.
The thought of an enderman blocking the narrow way is enough to make me pack a second working tool.
The End darkness is a poor time to discover a repair needs a steady bench.
The bridge leading toward the gateway matters more than the perfect repair when trouble is moving closer.
The edge of The Void would tell me which tool stays packed and which one stays ready.
You have convinced me to rethink the tool roll for The Void.
Did The Void leave more damage on the picks or on their handles?
I could build better gear for the next trip if I saw where this set wore down around The Void.
At The Void, I trust a plain tool that fits the hand better than a fine one that slips.
After hearing that story about The Void, I would give everyone one useful tool. Then nobody has to carry the whole workshop.
